key_insight: Marginal Advantage Accumulation (MAA) turns inconsistent batch-level memory feedback into comparable, cross-batch evidence so stable operations can be separated from accidental wins.
engineering_relevance: For memory-driven agent training, MAA offers a post-processing way to improve trace distillation quality while cutting optimization-phase token use by about 75%.
method: Build differential signals so operation feedback is comparable across batches
Accumulate signed per-operation evidence with EMA to track consistent advantage
Merge semantically identical traces to preserve cross-batch traceability
evidence_signal: Across 4 benchmarks and 4 target models, MAA achieved the best results in 14 of 16 settings, outperforming batch-level baselines and usually matching or exceeding online alternatives.
watch_item: Performance depends on reliable semantic identity merging and well-defined operation-level alignment, which may be sensitive to trace quality and implementation details.
paper_title: Marginal Advantage Accumulation for Memory-Driven Agent Self-Evolution
